title: Wombs and the stationary
theme: Some embodied beings go to a womb, others to the stationary state, according to their deeds and their learning.

words.context: Śaṅkara: «योनिद्वारं», the door of the womb
Śaṅkara: «अन्ये केचिदविद्यावन्तो मूढाः»; Raṅgarāmānuja: those turned away from hearing of the Supreme, unlike you, «परमात्मतत्त्वश्रवणविमुखाः त्वद्विसदृशाः»
Śaṅkara: «वृक्षादिस्थावरभावम्», the state of trees and the like
Śaṅkara: by the deeds done in this life, «यैर्यादृशं कर्म इह जन्मनि कृतं तद्वशेनेत्येतत्»

words.meaning: according to what they have learned
words.context: Śaṅkara: according to the knowledge gained, «यादृशं च विज्ञानमुपार्जितं तदनुरूपमेव शरीरं प्रतिपद्यन्त इत्यर्थः»

sandhi.rule: A final m remains before a vowel and is written joined to it.
After a word-final e an initial a is absorbed, marked by the avagraha, P. 6.1.109 (एङः पदान्तादति).

samasa.meaning: in accordance with what has been learned

morphology.note: The abstract noun in -tva from śarīra, in the dative of purpose: ‘for becoming a body’, ‘in order to be embodied’.
anu-sam-√i, present plural (yanti): ‘go along after, follow into’.

translation.literal: Some embodied ones enter a womb for embodiment; others follow into the stationary — according to their deeds, according to what they have learned.
translation.readable: Some embodied beings go to a womb to take a body again; others pass into things that do not move, such as trees — each according to what they have done and what they have come to know.

anvaya: अन्ये देहिनः शरीरत्वाय योनिम् प्रपद्यन्ते । अन्ये यथाकर्म यथाश्रुतम् स्थाणुम् अनुसंयन्ति ।
syntax: Two parallel clauses with anye … anye, ‘some … others’. The two adverbial compounds yathākarma yathāśrutam close the verse and qualify both clauses.

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: those without knowledge, «अविद्यावन्तो मूढाः», some of whom pass into wombs and the very lowest into plants. Raṅgarāmānuja: those turned away from hearing of the Supreme, unlike Naciketas, so that the verse sets off his fitness, «अधिकारिविशेषनिर्देशपरेण».

Śaṅkara: according to the knowledge acquired, citing a text as saying ‘births are according to understanding’, «‘यथाप्रज्ञं हि सम्भवाः’». Raṅgarāmānuja: according to the rites and meditations performed, citing the Chāndogya «'रमणीयचरणाः'» and the Bṛhadāraṇyaka «'तं विद्याकर्मणी समन्वारभेते'».

beginner: Death begins to answer the question about what happens after death, and he speaks of those who have not understood the teaching. Some take a new body through a womb; others, he says, go into the state of things that do not move, like trees. Which way each goes depends on two things: what they have done and what they have learned. The verse describes what the text teaches, and the commentators read it within their own frameworks. Śaṅkara says these are people without knowledge. Raṅgarāmānuja says Death mentions them to show how unlike them Naciketas is, since he wants to hear about the highest. Madhva says such going into wombs belongs to the individual self, never to Brahman.
analogy: Like travellers who each set out by the road their own steps have worn, one to a near town, one to a far one.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: Some embodied beings enter a womb to be embodied again; others go to the stationary state; each according to deeds and learning.

commentary.q: Śaṅkara: according to deed and understanding
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Those without knowledge enter a womb to take a body, «अन्ये केचिदविद्यावन्तो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते शरीरत्वाय शरीरग्रहणार्थं»; the very lowest go to the state of trees and the like, «स्थाणुं वृक्षादिस्थावरभावम्». Each takes a body according to the deeds done and knowledge gained; he cites «‘यथाप्रज्ञं हि सम्भवाः’», giving it as from the Aitareya Āraṇyaka.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Death speaks of those turned away from hearing of the Supreme, unlike Naciketas, «परमात्मतत्त्वश्रवणविमुखाः त्वद्विसदृशाः». They go to a womb or to the stationary state by the rites and meditations they have done, citing the Chāndogya and the Bṛhadāraṇyaka, «'तं विद्याकर्मणी समन्वारभेते'».

commentary.q: Madhva: this is the individual, not Brahman
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: In his comment filed under 2.1.2–3 (see the flags) he notes that going into wombs belongs to the individual self, not to Brahman, «न हि जीवस्य योन्यादिगमनं ब्रह्म».

commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: yathākarma and yathāśrutam are avyayībhāva compounds, adverbs formed with yathā, ‘according to’. Both qualify the two clauses together: the destination is fixed by deeds and by learning.

advaita.text: Those without knowledge take bodies according to deed and understanding, «यादृशं च विज्ञानमुपार्जितं तदनुरूपमेव शरीरं प्रतिपद्यन्त इत्यर्थः».

visistadvaita.text: The verse describes those turned away from the Supreme, to set off the pupil’s fitness, «परमात्मतत्त्वश्रवणविमुखाः त्वद्विसदृशाः».

dvaita.text: Going into wombs belongs to the individual self, which is other than Brahman, «न हि जीवस्य योन्यादिगमनं ब्रह्म».

schools.disagreement: All read the verse as describing the fate of those who do not know. Śaṅkara stresses deed and understanding; Raṅgarāmānuja the contrast with the fit pupil; Madhva the difference between the individual who is reborn and Brahman who is not.

parallels.note: The Chāndogya says that those of pleasant conduct enter a pleasant womb; Raṅgarāmānuja cites the passage.
Knowledge and deeds, and past understanding, take hold of the departing self; Raṅgarāmānuja cites it.
As one acts and behaves, so one becomes: the same principle as yathākarma.

contemporary.text: The verse joins what we do and what we learn as the two things that shape where we go. Whatever one makes of its account of rebirth, it treats learning as no less weighty than action. This is a reflection, not a claim made by the text.

reflect.beginner: Do you think what you learn shapes who you become as much as what you do?
reflect.deeper: Why might Raṅgarāmānuja read this verse as being about the pupil’s fitness rather than about others’ fate?
reflect.practice: Today, notice one thing you learned and one thing you did, and ask how each might shape tomorrow.

flags.note: Those who go to wombs and the stationary: the ignorant (Śaṅkara) or those turned from the Supreme, unlike Naciketas (Raṅgarāmānuja); yathāśrutam: knowledge gained (Śaṅkara) or rites and meditations (Raṅgarāmānuja).
Madhva’s comment on this verse is filed in madhva.json under 2.1.2–3 (see 2.2.6); it is cited here as madhva:2.1.2.
